title: Spaghetti Bolognese
subtitle: a slow-cooked meat ragu from Bologna
excerpt: A rich meat sauce that improves with every hour it cooks. Beef and pork mince simmer with wine and tomatoes until deeply savoury. Serve tossed through spaghetti with plenty of Parmesan.
sourceNotes: Ragu alla Bolognese originates from Bologna in Emilia-Romagna. The original uses minimal tomato and a long, slow cook over low heat.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the ragu in portions for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half for a quick weeknight meal.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The ragu tastes better the next day. Make it up to 3 days ahead and reheat gently.

content.text: The secret is patience. Cook the soffritto slowly and brown the mince in batches so it colours rather than steams. A long, gentle simmer builds depth.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pan over medium-low heat. Add the bacon and cook for 3 minutes until the fat renders. Add the onion, carrot and celery. Cook gently for 10 minutes until soft and golden.

Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Push the vegetables to the side. Turn the heat to high and add the beef mince. Spread it out and do not stir for 2 minutes. Let it colour before breaking it up. Repeat with the pork mince.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the red wine. Scrape up any bits from the bottom. Let it bubble and reduce by half, about 3 minutes.

Add the tinned tomatoes and bay leaves. Season well. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to very low. Cook uncovered for 60 to 90 minutes, stirring occasionally. The ragu should be thick and glossy.
Stir in the milk in the final 10 minutes if using. This softens any acidity and rounds out the flavour. Remove the bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Cook the pasta in a large pot of well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
Drain the pasta and add it to the ragu. Toss over low heat, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen. Serve in bowls with grated Parmesan.

items.cause: Heat too high or cooked too briefly
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer uncovered until reduced and thick.

items.cause: Pan was not hot enough when the mince went in
items.fix: Brown in smaller batches next time over high heat. Grey mince still tastes fine -- it just lacks depth.

items.cause: Tomatoes need longer cooking or acid from the wine
items.fix: Stir in the milk and cook for a further 10 minutes. A pinch of sugar also helps.

content.text: Bolognese comes from Bologna in northern Italy. The original ragu uses little tomato and a lot of meat. It is traditionally served with egg tagliatelle, not spaghetti. Both work well here.
